Governor Ivey Announces Alabama’s Mobile River Bridge Financing Named The Bond Buyer’s 2026 Southeast Deal of the Year

November 19, 2026

Press Releases

Share

Historic $3.786 billion financing recognized for innovative public finance structure supporting Alabama's largest infrastructure project

MONTGOMERY
 – Governor Kay Ivey on Thursday announced that financing for the Mobile River Bridge and Bayway Project has been named Southeast Deal of the Year by The Bond Buyer, one of the municipal finance industry’s leading publications. The $3.786 billion transaction, issued through the Alabama Toll Road, Bridge and Tunnel Authority, was recognized for its innovative financing structure and the collaboration required to advance one of the most significant infrastructure investments in Alabama’s history.

“This recognition reflects the tremendous effort it took to bring this long-awaited project to reality,” 
said Governor Ivey.
 “For decades, Alabamians have understood the need for a new Mobile River crossing, and through strong partnerships and a commitment to finding a financially responsible path forward, we are finally making that vision a reality. This investment will strengthen our Gulf Coast, support our growing economy and benefit generations of Alabamians. I am proud to see the innovative financing behind this historic project recognized on a national level.”

The recognition highlights the complexity and significance of the financing, which brought together multiple funding sources to make the long-planned Interstate 10 project financially viable. The transaction combines toll revenue bonds, a $2.52 billion federal Transportation Infrastructure Finance and Innovation Act (TIFIA) loan, federal grant funding and state support through an innovative financing structure designed to manage costs and risks while addressing the needs of local users.

The financing represents a major milestone in an effort that has spanned nearly three decades. Previous attempts to advance a new Mobile River crossing faced significant financial and public policy challenges. Through a revised approach that incorporated state and federal support, regional collaboration and a more affordable tolling structure, Alabama was able to develop an investment-grade financing plan and move the project into construction.

“This recognition is a testament to the tremendous work and collaboration that went into bringing this financing together,” 
said State Finance Director Doryan Carlton
. “A project of this scale requires careful financial planning, innovative thinking and coordination among numerous state, federal and local partners. The financing structure demonstrates how those resources can be brought together to address complex infrastructure needs while positioning Alabama for continued economic growth.”

The transaction is particularly notable for its combination of financing tools. The $2.52 billion TIFIA loan is the largest ever awarded through the federal program.

The Bond Buyer will recognize the transaction as the Southeast region’s Deal of the Year as part of its 2026 annual awards program. The awards recognize notable municipal finance transactions for innovation and their contributions to the communities and public purposes served by the municipal bond market. The Southeast recognition also places the Alabama transaction among the 10 regional and category honorees selected nationally as finalists for the publication’s overall 2026 Deal of the Year award, which will be announced December 1.

The financing will support the $3.2 billion Phase One project of the Mobile River Bridge and Bayway Project, which includes construction of a new six-lane cable-stayed bridge over the Mobile River, improvements to key interchanges and traffic flow, and restriping of the existing Bayway to provide six lanes of capacity across Mobile Bay. The project is intended to improve mobility along one of the Gulf Coast’s most important transportation corridors, strengthen connections between Mobile and Baldwin counties, support the Port of Mobile and enhance regional commerce and emergency evacuation capabilities.

After nearly 30 years of planning, coordination and financial development, construction officially began in October 2026 with a groundbreaking ceremony in Mobile attended by Governor Ivey, other state, federal and local leaders.
